clue.text: One who may have to wait for money

definitions.text: One who may have to wait for money

parts.words: One who may have to wait for money
parts.note: to wait is to serve at table, and a paid domestic does just that for wages

explanation.surface: Someone kept hanging about until they get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait' reads as standing around till payday, but in the sense of waiting at table it describes a paid domestic.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic employee waits on others in return for wages.

clue.text: Man with a pistol beginning to hesitate

parts.note: a beginning is a start
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A gunman is starting to falter.
explanation.walkthrough: The man with a pistol is not a gunman but the official who fires the gun to begin a race.
explanation.definitionFit: At a race the official who fires a pistol to set the runners off has this title.

clue.text: Rise and fall on the wash like a kind of herring

parts.note: a ship rolls, rising and falling on the swell
to mop is to wash a floor

explanation.surface: Something bobbing up and down on the tide like a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled fillet of pickled fish, a common deli item.

clue.text: Great annoyance when fisherman gets left out

indicators.note: out says that a letter is to be dropped from the fisherman word

parts.note: an angler is a rod fisherman

explanation.surface: A fisherman is furious at being excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets left out' removes L from ANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Great annoyance is rage or wrath.

clue.text: The first French painter to show a bride's outfit

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word The

parts.note: Henri Rousseau was a French naive painter

explanation.surface: A French artist is the first to display a wedding dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The clothes and linen a bride assembles for her marriage.

clue.text: Ring a friend about twitch in the eye

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: about means the friend word goes around the twitch word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Phoning a friend about an eye twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring a friend' looks like making a phone call; it is O followed by PAL wrapped around TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical describes what concerns sight and the visual organ.

clue.text: Skips are very large with German in!

indicators.note: in places the German word inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: Big skips containing a German.
explanation.walkthrough: Skips look like rubbish containers but the definition is the verb: leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to leave it out or pass over it.

clue.text: Assess the situation with the eyes of a thief

definitions.meaning: to review where things stand before acting

definitions.text: with the eyes of a thief
definitions.meaning: a thief sees goods as stock to be carried off

explanation.surface: Weighing things up the way a burglar would.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviewing one's position; for a thief, literally removing a shop's goods.

clue.text: Greek character who is against Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means opposed

explanation.surface: A Greek who opposes the wine of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Support for a member

parts.note: a member is a limb, and the support is a rest placed under it

explanation.surface: Backing given to a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a club or party, but here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion or stool propping up a limb.

clue.text: Term which is musical or legal perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of or legal could form another word

explanation.surface: A word that might belong to music or to law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OR LEGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempo marking meaning lively and fast.

clue.text: A suggestion of a dark liquid on the fish

parts.note: ink is a dark writing fluid
ling is a sea fish related to cod

explanation.surface: A hint of squid ink spilt on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint hint or slight idea.

clue.text: Bushes present a mother with danger in Back St

indicators.note: in places the mother and danger pieces within the street abbreviation
Back means the street abbreviation is read in the opposite order

parts.note: St is short for street
ma is a word for mother
a risk is a danger

explanation.surface: Shrubs present a risky prospect for a mum in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back St' looks like an alley; 'Back' turns ST into TS, which then holds A MA RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathery shrubs that grow by the sea.

clue.text: Cause a black mark by an error on two notes

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or error
G is a note of the musical scale
E is another note of the scale

explanation.surface: A mistake on two notes earns a black mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A black mark sounds like a reprimand; here it is a scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch lightly, leaving a burn.

clue.text: Rent raised, causing a forced split

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
up means raised

explanation.surface: A rent rise leads to a messy break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear to pieces by force.

clue.text: One and all included in the party, but not totally

indicators.note: included in means the one and all pieces go inside the party word

parts.note: a party is a social gathering
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Everyone was invited, but the party was only half a success.
explanation.definitionFit: In part only; to some extent.

clue.text: Person responsible for changes to incomes

definitions.text: Person responsible for changes to incomes

parts.words: Person responsible for changes to incomes
parts.note: a specialist in finance who shapes policy affecting earnings

explanation.surface: Whoever is to blame for pay changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Changes to incomes hints at an anagram, and INCOMES is part of the letters, but the clue works as a description of a financial expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in the study of money, production and wealth advises on pay and taxation.

clue.text: Pull this out to start the music

definitions.text: Pull this out to start the music

parts.words: Pull this out to start the music
parts.note: a knob on a church instrument that is drawn out to make pipes sound

explanation.surface: An instruction for starting a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The image is of a church organ, where drawing out a knob lets a rank of pipes sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob on a pipe instrument that controls a set of pipes.

clue.text: UN ordered to drug hen with protruding lower jaw

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of UN, drug and hen are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The United Nations instructed to sedate a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the UN giving a command; it rearranges UN DRUG HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the lower jaw jutting beyond the upper one.

clue.text: Put dead letters aside to be revised

indicators.note: letters aside asks for the letters of put dead to be set out afresh

explanation.surface: Unwanted post is set aside for review.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead letters are undeliverable mail, but 'letters aside' rearranges PUT DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought up to date, revised with current information.

clue.text: Cover up for a girl in a difficult spot

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the cover word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Covering for a girl lands someone in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' looks like hiding the truth; 'up' turns LID into DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicament involving a hard choice.

clue.text: Recoils at use of boots

definitions.meaning: a gun jerks back when fired

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at being booted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's jerk back on firing; also blows with the feet.

clue.text: First class wild orchid I plucked off last March was ring shaped

indicators.note: First takes the opening letter of class
wild means the remaining letters are scrambled
plucked off says a letter is pulled away from orchid I
last takes the final letter of March

explanation.surface: A wild orchid picked last March was round in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plucked off' removes H (the last letter of March) from ORCHID I, and 'wild' shuffles ORCIDI into RICOID after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricoid describes the ring-like cartilage of the larynx.

clue.text: She will shortly get a bill for some varnish

parts.note: she will shortened is she'll
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: She'll soon receive an invoice for varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but signals the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin dissolved in alcohol used as a finish on wood.

clue.text: I held assembly in Indian city

indicators.note: assembly means putting the letters of I held together in a new order

explanation.surface: I hosted a gathering in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a meeting; it rearranges I HELD.
explanation.definitionFit: India's capital territory.

clue.text: Show annoyance when bit of fork catches fruit

indicators.note: catches means the fork part holds the annoyance word inside

parts.note: a tine is a prong of a fork
to anger is to annoy

explanation.surface: Being cross when a fork prong spears fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small orange citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Number might be there

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters of there could become something else

explanation.surface: A figure might be over there.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number, one more than two.

clue.text: Don't start fear by mistake

indicators.note: Don't start tells us to drop the opening letter of the fear word

parts.note: terror is great fear

explanation.surface: Being told not to panic by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or blunder.

clue.text: The glass falls

parts.note: a drinking vessel, and also one who falls about as an acrobat does

explanation.surface: The barometer is dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The glass falls' suggests a falling barometer, but it describes a drinking vessel and an acrobat who takes falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed drinking vessel; also an acrobat who somersaults.

clue.text: Rum mixture in work can cause great confusion

indicators.note: in places the mixed rum letters inside the work word

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: mixture means the letters of rum are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rum cocktail at work causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges RUM into URM, which goes in TOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of upheaval and disorder.

clue.text: Filter operates easily after first day

indicators.note: after puts the reworked letters behind the day letter
first takes the opening letter of day
operates suggests the letters of easily are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A filter works smoothly after the first day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operates' rearranges EASILY into IALYSE, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate substances through a membrane, as a kidney machine does.

clue.text: Picador is ludicrous!

indicators.note: is ludicrous says the letters of picador are made absurd by being jumbled

explanation.surface: A bullfighter on horseback is laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ludicrous' rearranges PICADOR; the whole clue says such a mockery is ludicrous.
explanation.definitionFit: Parodic means mocking by imitation, making something seem ludicrous.
